newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Liton limit up on ex-bonus issue.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Liton limit up on ex-bonus issue.

text.p: Taiwan's Liton Electronic, one of the market's current bellwether electronics and China-concept shares, surged in early Wednesday trade on an announcement of a bonus issue, brokers said.
Opto-electronics and power supply maker Liton on Wednesday released a bonus issue, or stock dividend of T$2 per share for 1996, paying 200 shares free for every 1,000 shares held.
After 55 minutes, at 0155 GMT, Liton had risen the daily seven percent limit to T$106, while the overall index was up 0.41 percent.

"Being both an electronics and China-concept share, Liton is surely a target of bargain hunters, especially in the face of their ex-bonus issue," said Golden Securities research chief Albert Lin. "Liton still has room to rise further."
Most electronics shares, through with their ex-bonus issues recently, had soared due to heavy buying.

China-concept shares -- Taiwan firms with active or planned investments in the communist mainland -- had also surged recently to reflect big gains by Hong Kong's China-linked shares ahead of the British colony's July 1 handover to Beijing.
